threat.name: Covid Contact Tracing Info Sold (Netherlands)
threat.description: Information collected by the Dutch government for covid contact tracing was leaked and sold online
threat.fullDescription: Millions of records from the CoronIT and HPZone systems used in the Netherlands to track, respectively, corona test results and contact tracing information; have been sold and exchanged between criminals.

threatcharacteristic.name: Storage/processing personal data
threatcharacteristic.description: Storage and processing of extensive amounts of personal data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Transfer of personal information to third parties but legitimate users of the system.
threatcharacteristic.description: Legitimate users had access to all the data and could export it. As a result, this sensitive data was sold by malicious insiders. This threat would not necessarily be found with the classic STRIDE information disclosure threat as there was no breach of the system.

threatcharacteristic.name: Storage/processing personal data
threatcharacteristic.description: Storage and processing of personal data pertaining an excessive number of data subjects.

threat.name: Facebook Data Leak (500 Million Records)
threat.description: Facebook data leak of 500 million people’s records.
threat.fullDescription: In 2021, a data leak at social media platform Facebook led to the unauthorized disclosure of over 500 million records, including full names, phone numbers, locations and birth dates of the involved data subjects.

threatcharacteristic.name: Data disclosed by data subject
threatcharacteristic.description: Data containing identity details is directly collected from the data subject.

threatcharacteristic.name: Stored for a long time
threatcharacteristic.description: This breach also affected former users who already had their account deleted. Despite this 'deletion', the social network had retained their data after all, which meant they were still affected by the breach.

threatcharacteristic.name: Query interface for phone numbers
threatcharacteristic.description: The dataset could be queried for phone number, allowing to find the corresponding user account. In this way, an adversary could use the phone number as a unique identifier to link accounts to actual data subjects, and potentially other data that is known about this person.

threat.name: Browser Fingerprinting
threat.description: A profile of the browser is constructed by relying on numerous quasi-identifiers and derived properties.
threat.fullDescription: Various characteristics of a user's browser (such as screen resolution, installed plugins, user agent, etc.) can be used to form a unique fingerprint of this browser and therefore identify the user across multiple websites.

threatcharacteristic.name: Browser properties as quasi-identifiers
threatcharacteristic.description: A combination of browser properties can be used as a quasi-identifier. For example, the user agent, language, window size, extensions, supported features, etc.

threatcharacteristic.name: Derive fingerprint
threatcharacteristic.description: A fingerprint can be derived by rendering text and graphics and exploiting the fact that different physical devices will render these slightly differently. This allows distinguishing physcal devices, and by extension the users of said devices, from others.

threat.name: Social network gap
threat.description: Social network tracking data subjects that do not have an account at this service
threat.fullDescription: Regardless of a user’s presence on a social network, these networks can learn a lot about that user by combining the information they learn indirectly through the other users.

threatcharacteristic.name: Combine indirect links
threatcharacteristic.description: Indirect links to the person not present on the network are combined. (Person is present in contact list of existing users on the network.)

threatcharacteristic.name: Data subject unaware their data is being processed
threatcharacteristic.description: The data subject does not know their data is being processed, as they never interacted with the social network. Their information is processed via the profiles of their friends.

threat.name: DB Query inference
threat.description: Information obtained from consecutive DB queries can be used for profiling data subjects
threat.fullDescription: By querying a database for multiple different pieces of information, further data could be inferred than what is strictly stored in the database. This could then be used to profile data subjects or learn sensitive information.

threatcharacteristic.name: Targeted queries
threatcharacteristic.description: Multiple queries to a database can be used to learn more information by combining the results of these queries to infer additional knowledge.

threatcharacteristic.name: Linkable Dataset
threatcharacteristic.description: Data points in the dataset can be linked. Using this linked data together with (dis)similarities between users, it may become possible to learn sensitive information about the data subject.

threat.name: Machine learning
threat.description: Profiling users based on machine learning techniques
threat.fullDescription: Machine learning techniques can be used to automatically construct profiles by combining multiple elements to link information to data subjects. For example, some AI models can be used to profile people based on the contents and writing style of their search prompts.

threatcharacteristic.name: Directly derived linkable properties
threatcharacteristic.description: Linkable properties are derived directly from the data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Indirectly derived linkable properties
threatcharacteristic.description: Linkable properties are indirectly derived through message and timing patterns.

threat.name: Reusing username linked to identity
threat.description: A data subject reusing a username that is already previously linked to their identity
threat.fullDescription: When reusing a username across multiple websites, or even a username that contains the actual name of the data subject, a person might inadvertently be identified on multiple services even if they only revealed their true identity on one of these services.

threatcharacteristic.name: Username is linked to identity
threatcharacteristic.description: The username is already linked to the identity.

threatcharacteristic.name: Linking accounts across multiple services
threatcharacteristic.description: Accounts can be linked across services because they have the same username

threat.name: Attributing Whistleblower Submission
threat.description: Attributability of documents to a specific person can lead to prosecution/firing/... of whistleblowers.
threat.fullDescription: Metadata stored in a document or in an action log can lead to attributing a (leaked) document back to a specific person. This can in turn lead to the prosecution, termination, ... of whistleblowers.

threatcharacteristic.name: Logged communication
threatcharacteristic.description: The communication of an employee with the whistleblower submission system may be logged.

threatcharacteristic.name: Meta-data to link back to the whistleblower
threatcharacteristic.description: Meta-data in the submitted document may expose additional information that can be used to trace back to the whistleblower.

threatcharacteristic.name: Attributable action
threatcharacteristic.description: The action of leaking may be attributed because the information the whistleblower submits is tailored to the whistleblower and can subsequently be attributed to that person.

threat.name: Attributed E-vote
threat.description: Votes in a flawed digital voting system can potentially be attributed to the user to enable coercion/compensation/..
threat.fullDescription: E-voting poses many challenges, such as building a robust system in which votes can never be attributed to the person who submitted it. In a flawed e-voting system, votes could be attributrd back to the voters, posing grave privacy challenges and potentially compromising the vote itself.

threatcharacteristic.name: Attribute vote
threatcharacteristic.description: A vote can be attributed to the person making the vote. Published with an id linked to the voter.

threatcharacteristic.name: Signed receipts
threatcharacteristic.description: Signed receipts can be used to prove a vote was cast a certain way.

threat.name: Geo-tagged photos
threat.description: Image files potentially contain metadata revealing personal data such as location details
threat.fullDescription: Geolocation data stored in image files may inadvertently reveal information about the person who took the picture (e.g., where they live, where they work, which devices they own, etc.)

threatcharacteristic.name: Location information in meta-data
threatcharacteristic.description: Location information in photos can provide additional information to make it harder to deny claims about the location a user has been.

threatcharacteristic.name: Unawareness of person taking photo that location is stored
threatcharacteristic.description: The person taking the picture may not know their geolocation is collected and stored within the metadata of the photo.

threat.name: DKIM
threat.description: DKIM signatures could be used by an adversary to try to prove legitimacy of a stolen sent email
threat.fullDescription: DKIM provides long-term proof of authenticity for emails which enables adversaries that have stolen emails to prove their legitimacy in trying to, for example, blackmail a victim.

threatcharacteristic.name: Email signed by domain
threatcharacteristic.description: Email messages contain signatures of the sending email server.

threatcharacteristic.name: Email signature in meta-data
threatcharacteristic.description: Email signature information is contained in the meta-data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Evidence of having sent email
threatcharacteristic.description: Signed message by email provider provides evidence of having sent email.

threatcharacteristic.name: Unawareness of digital signature
threatcharacteristic.description: The sender of an email may not be aware that their emails are being digitally signed and can be used for non-repudiation.

threat.name: Profiling Revealing Sensitive Attributes In Advertisements
threat.description: Targeted advertising based on the data subject's profiled attributes may reveal sensitive information about the person.
threat.fullDescription: The profiling of an individual can reveal sensitive attributes via the targeted ads that individual receives. For example, these ads may reveal sensitive attributes such as pregnancy, sexual orientation, etc.

threatcharacteristic.name: Previous actions are profiled
threatcharacteristic.description: By being assigned to a certain profiled group, the data subject may no longer deny certain claims about them. For example, a person consistently getting ads for a gambling site may no longer be able to hide that they frequented such websites in the past.

threatcharacteristic.name: Types of ads served
threatcharacteristic.description: The type of ads servied to the user reveal sensitive attributes.

threatcharacteristic.name: Profiling the individual for targeted advertising
threatcharacteristic.description: The data subject is profiled in order to target them with personalised ads. This profiling may reveal (sensitive) attributes about the data subject, such as their medical history or political views.

threat.name: Publishing Watermarked Information
threat.description: Watermarks in leaked/published documents may reveal personal information about who published it.
threat.fullDescription: Watermarking technologies such as printer dots can lead to attributing a (leaked) document back to a specific person. This can in turn lead to the prosecution, termination, ... of whistleblowers.

threatcharacteristic.name: Attribute data to recipient
threatcharacteristic.description: The publishing of the watermarked information can be attributed to the individual that received the data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Meta-data to attribute recipient
threatcharacteristic.description: The data can contain meta-data to attribute the recipient of the data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Embedded data on the recipient
threatcharacteristic.description: The published information can contain hidden patterns or watermarks to track the origin of the data.

threat.name: Linkedin contact suggestion reveals profile viewers
threat.description: LinkedIn suggests you to connect with a person, because that person looked you up.
threat.fullDescription: Professional social network LinkedIn has a feature that suggest connections based on who visited your profile (and in some cases outright reveals that a person visited your profile). A person who knows such suggestions are based on profile visits may deduce that the suggested people visited their profile at some point in the past.

threatcharacteristic.name: Attribution of actions due to side-effects
threatcharacteristic.description: Appearing in the suggested connections of a person based on profile views is a side effect of the action of viewing someones profile.

threatcharacteristic.name: Data subject is unaware their visit to someone's profile is disclosed to that person
threatcharacteristic.description: The person visiting someone's profile may not be aware that this action may cause a side effect that indicates to the other person that they visited their profile.

threat.name: Traditional encrypted data volumes reveal the existence of data
threat.description: Having an encrypted data volume shows the presence of data, potentially including the amount of data
threat.fullDescription: By detecting the existence of an encrypted data volume, an attacker could coerce the data owner into revealing the password by force. Hidden encrypted volumes can provide a solution to this, as the owner of the data can plausibly deny the existence of the data stored within the volume.

threatcharacteristic.name: Data owner cannot deny existence of the encrypted information
threatcharacteristic.description: The owner of the data cannot deny the existence of the data stored in a traditional encrypted data volume.

threatcharacteristic.name: Use of encryption software creates a detectable encrypted data volume
threatcharacteristic.description: The use of encryption software to create an encrypted data volume enables the detection of this volume. This reveals the existence of the data, and potentially leaks how much data is stored within it.

threat.name: Contact tracing
threat.description: Detecting over bluetooth whether someone is running contact tracing application.
threat.fullDescription: COVID-19 contact tracing apps transmit short randomized tokens periodically. By receiving such a token in an area with very few other people, the original sender of such a token may be identified again by those who received the token. In doing so, the observer can infer that a person is using the tracing application, and this can potentially be linked at a later time to other data points, for example to try to link a positive test result to a specific person.

threatcharacteristic.name: Observable bluetooth LE signal
threatcharacteristic.description: Bluetooth LE signals can be observed and intercepted by anyone within range.
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The presence of the bluetooth LE signal used for contact tracing can be detected by anyone within range, therefore enabling them to learn that a person is in the area and that they are running the contact tracing application.

threatcharacteristic.name: Inference of token sender
threatcharacteristic.description: The observer can infer who sent a detected token by linking to contextual data
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The observer of the sent token can infer who the sender is if there are not that many others in the same area by linking the detection to contextual data.

threat.name: SSO provider can link service use
threat.description: An SSO service provider can link users' usages of different services.
threat.fullDescription: Single-sign on providers receive information about the user's logins on multiple different other services, as they are acting as the identity provider in this situation. This puts them in a central position to link logins together and learn which services the data subject uses. This reveals more (potentially sensitive) personal information about the user.

threatcharacteristic.name: SSO identifiers
threatcharacteristic.description: SSO uses unique identifiers for performing the single sign on, which enables linking sign on requests for different services to each other and track the user across multiple platforms.

threatcharacteristic.name: Overprocessing of data by the SSO provider
threatcharacteristic.description: The SSO provider processes the personal data for purposes not necessary to deliver the sign-on service
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The SSO provider potentially processes the personal data for purposes other than delivery of the sign-on service (e.g., tracking the user across multiple services by linking their logins).

threat.name: FLoC Browser tracking
threat.description: Federated Learning of Cohorts (FLoC) privacy sandboxing profiles users based on their browsing history
threat.fullDescription: The FLoC privacy sandbox, while marketed as a privacy enhancing technology, has received criticism that it has design flaws that may allow for profiling and tracking of users based on their Cohort ID

threatcharacteristic.name: Track activity to local user
threatcharacteristic.description: Link local browsing activity to a user.

threatcharacteristic.name: Analyze browsing data for patterns
threatcharacteristic.description: Analyze and link browsing data through patterns to assign FLoC cohort.

threatcharacteristic.name: Indirectly link through others in FLoC cohort.
threatcharacteristic.description: Indirectly link browsing behavior through other users in the cohort

threatcharacteristic.name: User is profiled locally
threatcharacteristic.description: The user is profiled locally on their own device

threat.name: Password managers automatically fills in identifying information
threat.description: By automatically filling in personal information, the information is available for java script running in the page to retrieve and process it.
threat.fullDescription: Some websites already collect information filled in a webform even before it is submitted. This means that auto-filled information (e.g., by a password manager), could already be collected even if the user never intended to click submit on the form.

threatcharacteristic.name: Page contains forms fields for personal data
threatcharacteristic.description: Form fields requesting personal data are present.

threatcharacteristic.name: Webpage scripts proces the information that is entered locally
threatcharacteristic.description: Scripts in the page can already access the information entered in the form fields before submission.

threat.name: Logging actions
threat.description: Logging user actions prevents plausible deniability.
threat.fullDescription: Event or action logs can be used to prove that a user has taken certain actions, leaving them a weakened plausible deniability (or none at all, depending on the strength/credibility of the logs).

threatcharacteristic.name: Action logging
threatcharacteristic.description: Taking certain actions in the system may lead to that action being logged as a side-effect.

threatcharacteristic.name: Logged data causes non-repudiation
threatcharacteristic.description: Logged data makes it harder (or impossible) to deny certain actions have taken place.

threat.name: Context data from wearable or implanted (smart) devices
threat.description: Observing communications from wearable or implanted (smart) devices may reveal that a person nearby is using such device.
threat.fullDescription: Observing communications from wearable or implanted (smart) devices such as a smartwatch, or even a smart pacemaker or insulin pump, may reveal that a person nearby is using such device. This can in turn leak additional information about the person, for example that they have a specific medical condition.

threatcharacteristic.name: Contextual data from sensors in communication meta-data
threatcharacteristic.description: Contextual data form sensors in communication meta-data can lead to detectability threats.

threatcharacteristic.name: Inferred sensitive information from context data
threatcharacteristic.description: Using contextual data to infer more about a data subject may lead to the unwanted discovery of sensitive information.

threat.name: Linkable data from multiple users
threat.description: Data from multiple users are linked by by combining multiple records or datasets.
threat.fullDescription: When data from multiple individuals is combined, this can be used to profile them as a group. For example, comparing records of people living in the same neighborhood may lead to attributes (such as income level, energy consumption, etc.) being assigned to the entire neighborhood altogether.

threatcharacteristic.name: Linking data from separate data subjects
threatcharacteristic.description: Data points pertaining different data subjects within the data set are linked in order to create new knowledge.

threatcharacteristic.name: Inferring information about a group of data subjects at once.
threatcharacteristic.description: The inferred information about multiple individuals is used to profile the group of people as a whole.

threat.name: Push notification payloads expose sensitive information
threat.description: The payload field of push notifications is often not encrypted, which leads to overexposure of the potentially sensitive data within it.
threat.fullDescription: While most push notification service providers such as Apple Push Notification Service (APNs), or Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) strongly recommend the encryption of the payload of push notifications to mobile phones, this is quite often neglected. When this payload is not encrypted, sensitive data such as the contents of personal messages can be exposed to the providers of such services. Often, the owner of the mobile device is not aware that the contents of their notifications may be overly exposed.

threatcharacteristic.name: Data excessively available to push notification providers
threatcharacteristic.description: The unencrypted payloads of push notifications cause the information within to be overly accessible (i.e., to the providers of push notification services).
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The unencrypted payloads of push notifications cause the information within to be overly accessible (i.e., to the providers of push notification services).

threatcharacteristic.name: User is unaware of overexposure of their data
threatcharacteristic.description: The user is often not aware that the push notification service provider has access to the unencrypted payload data.
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The user is often not aware that the push notification service provider has access to the unencrypted payload data.

threatcharacteristic.name: Lacking Encryption indicates insufficient cybersecurity risk management
threatcharacteristic.description: The lack of encryption of notification payloads is an indication that the system was not designed according to cyber security standards and best practices.
threatcharacteristic.fullDescription: The lack of encryption of notification payloads is an indication that the system was not designed according to cyber security standards and best practices.
